newsitem.title: USA: Acme Q1 hurt by costs, depreciation.
newsitem.headline: Acme Q1 hurt by costs, depreciation.

text.p: Acme Metals Inc said its first-quarter loss reflects inefficient operations during its continued commissioning of a new steel making facility and the ongoing phaseout of old facilities.
The steel making segment posted an operating loss of $19.9 million compared to operating income of $300,000 last year. The segment incurred about $10 million in cost inefficiencies.

Also hurting performance in the quarter was an increase in depreciation of $6.8 million and $11 million in net interest expense associated with the new Compact Strip Production facility that began operations in the 1996 fourth quarter.
Earlier Thursday, Acme Metals posted a first-quarter net loss of $15.9 million or $1.36 per share compared to a year-earlier profit of $3.4 million or $0.30 per share.

President Stephen Bennett said the company's Acme Packaging Corp continues with its plan to install new plastic strapping manufacturing lines later this year. In the steel making segment, Bennett said, "We are continuing with the commissioning and fine tuning of new equipment. Shipments from the new facility accounted for 37 percent of our first quarter shipments, up from five percent in the fourth quarter."
